comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Calibration complete (code-v3, 1760 sidecars / 1173 changes / 4359 findings). Recommendation (precision-first; EVERY would-block finding validity>=0.95, none <0.5):

FLIP TO BLOCKING:
- regression @ 0.54 (n=307, val 0.83, drop 0.17, rev_rr 0.68/93eps; blocks 2.81% of changes)
- api-compat @ 0.51 (n=118, val 0.88, rev_rr 0.75/34eps; 0.77%)
- deletion-impact @ 0.60 (n=73, val 0.88, rev_rr 0.66/21eps; 0.26%)
- error-handling @ 0.50 (n=238, val 0.83, rev_rr 0.64/55eps; 0.26%, low-yield but precise)

HOLD ADVISORY: performance (rev_rr 0.85 rests on only 12 episodes; would block 1 finding — insufficient evidence).
KEEP: security @ 0.54 as-is (code-v3 confirms precise, 0.26% of changes). High-volume tests/maintainability/correctness/edge-cases stay advisory (rev_rr<0.6, blocking the ~0.30 priority mode = high friction).
KEEP ADVISORY (FP-prone, high decider drop): docs 76%, supply-chain 64%, scope-intent 58%.
NOT TUNABLE (DET/attestation): bugfix-size-attestation, secret-detection, sec.

Caveat: a held-out (human/Sonnet) adjudication of the would-block sets should confirm before flipping in production, exactly as code-v2 deferred security to sibling b9c0. Full report + harness in session workspace. Landing (harness -> docs/experiments/, criteria_routing.json edits) pending operator go-ahead + the claim->review-plan->Gerrit workflow.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Escaped-bug analysis (43 close_class=regression bugs, correlated to prior PASS reviews of the buggy file with defect-level identifier matching):

(a) Would non-blocking findings have caught them? A finding existed for 8/43, but only 1/8 would flip to a BLOCK under the APPROVED thresholds:
- autumnal-defectible-xeme ('rebar metrics' with no dates crashes): advisory regression prio 0.60 >= 0.54 -> WOULD BLOCK. Validates the regression flip.
- The other 7 sat at prio 0.0-0.30 or were DROPPED by the Pass-3 decider (brattish-ladyish-jaguar: correct finding dropped at val 0.43). Threshold-tightening is NOT the lever for that tail.
Two non-threshold levers surfaced: (i) verifier RECALL (correct-but-dropped findings on regression/edge-cases); (ii) a targeted impact boost for deletion-impact/api-compat findings that cite a removed public symbol + a named broken caller (citric-preregal-ladybird sat at 0.30, below the 0.60/0.51 flips).

(b) Criteria gaps (recurring escaped classes with NO relevant finding): import/packaging resolution integrity (~4), CI-gate rollout backward-compat (~4), CLI<->MCP<->import-format surface parity (~3; halfwhite-chordal-stonefly had 9 PASS reviews and zero findings), live/external-integration signatures (~4, out of scope for static review). Proposing new overlays: import-integrity (or expand deletion-impact to import-graph breakage), surface-parity, ci-gate-compat. Full report in session workspace.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Cross-epic interaction with RP-06 (uneducated-habitual-primate), specifically S1 `dietetic-pompous-boar` "Compile immutable effective review-policy snapshots".

S1 creates an immutable repository-bound `CriteriaSnapshot` in `rebar.llm.criteria` that folds effective built-ins + project LLM/DET criteria + routing/posture/applicability into ONE authority, replacing today's "packaged-only overlay and detector registries" reads (its stated defect: "a project disable or RETUNE can be ignored"). Its file_impact includes new `llm/criteria/{snapshot,overlay}.py` and `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`.

This calibration edits the PACKAGED `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` (flips api-compat/deletion-impact/regression/error-handling to blocking). That packaged routing is exactly what S1 restructures the consumption of.

Relationship = landing-order COORDINATION, not a blocking dependency:
- S1's golden contract tests pin "current behavior … allow only the approved corrections." If these calibrated blocking thresholds are not present when S1 captures its baseline, S1 will either flag them as an unapproved delta or the new snapshot silently drops the retune.
- Whichever lands first, the other side must preserve the calibrated thresholds: land these flips before S1's golden capture, OR have S1 include them in its approved baseline.

Linked `relates_to` S1 (dietetic-pompous-boar) to make this visible to whoever executes either side. No relationship to the write-parity siblings (scratchy/topaz/blusterous/churlish/linen) — those touch the write-op adapter subsystem, disjoint from RP-06's review-gate discovery subsystem (no shared files, no behavioral coupling).

compiled_state.description:
Land the operator-approved code-review criteria threshold flips derived from the code-v3 sidecar calibration. The analysis is COMPLETE (see this ticket's comments: 1760 code_review_result_v2 sidecars / 1173 changes / 4359 findings, calibrated per-criterion, precision-first). This ticket lands the recommendation the operator has cleared.

## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` currently blocks only on the two DET security detectors + the `security` AGENT criterion (b9c0). Every other LLM criterion is advisory@0.95, so high-precision defect classes the code-v3 corpus shows are safe to block (validity>=0.95 on every would-block finding, low change-blocking volume) never gate a review. The calibration recommended flipping four to blocking; the operator has approved landing them.

## Approach
Edit the packaged `criteria_routing.json` to flip exactly four criteria from advisory to blocking at their calibrated thresholds, each annotated with a `_comment` citing this ticket + the code-v3 calibration:
- api-compat -> blocking @ 0.51 (n=118, validity 0.88; break-in-caller API changes, high-precision/low-volume)
- deletion-impact -> blocking @ 0.60 (n=73, validity 0.88; a dangling reference to a removed def/class/signature)
- regression -> blocking @ 0.54 (base-reviewer dimension, n=307, validity 0.83) — NEW key
- error-handling -> blocking @ 0.50 (base-reviewer dimension, n=238, validity 0.83) — NEW key
`security` stays as-is; performance/docs/supply-chain/scope-intent and the high-volume dimensions stay advisory (insufficient evidence or high friction). The two `regression`/`error-handling` entries are BASE-REVIEWER dimensions (not glob overlays in OVERLAY_IDS): `exec`/`applies_to` are inert and only `default_posture`/`block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` are consulted by `registry.threshold_for`.

Update the three governance-pin tests that assert the exact approved blocking set (previously the 3-member {secret-detection, high-critical-security, security}) to the new 7-member set, so the "adding a blocking criterion must be a deliberate re-approved change" guard still holds at the new baseline.

## Portability
Pure in-process threshold config consumed by `registry.threshold_for`; no CI provider or external trigger involved, so the change is fully portable across environments with diverse or no CI (project.portability unaffected).

## Sequencing
Land BEFORE RP-06 S1 (dietetic-pompous-boar, relates_to): S1 folds this packaged `criteria_routing.json` into an immutable CriteriaSnapshot golden, so S1 must derive its golden from the flipped file. S1 is still open, so no golden re-derivation is required here.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json — flip the four criteria (2 edited entries + 2 new base-dimension keys).
- tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py — repoint the deletion-impact routing assertion to (0.60, True).
- tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py — expand the approved-blocking-set pin to the 7 members.
- tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py — expand the approved-blocking-set pin to the 7 members.
(The calibration/analysis harness under docs/experiments/ is a local investigation aid and is NOT part of this landing.)

## Testing
- The three updated governance tests pass and now pin the 7-member blocking set (any 8th addition must be deliberately re-approved).
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py` green.
- The broader code-review routing/registry unit tests stay green (no criterion resolves to a different threshold than declared).
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] api-compat, deletion-impact, regression, error-handling are blocking_enabled=true at 0.51/0.60/0.54/0.50 respectively in the packaged criteria_routing.json, each with a `_comment` citing cranial-goodly-seahog + the code-v3 calibration.
- [x] `security` and the two DET detectors remain blocking; no other criterion is flipped (the approved blocking set is exactly 7 members).
- [x] regression and error-handling are added as base-reviewer dimension entries (applies_to=[], only posture/threshold/blocking_enabled consulted).
- [x] The three governance-pin tests assert the new 7-member set and pass.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` are green.
